Best time to visit

Wildlife does not follow a single high season across four countries. Use this as a planning calendar, then tell us the month you can actually travel.

JanuaryStrong

Hot and dry in much of Kenya. Amboseli often has clear Kilimanjaro dawns. Calving begins on the southern Serengeti.

FebruaryStrong

Peak calving on the short-grass plains. Predator watching is excellent. Kenya parks are dry and dusty.

MarchGood

A shoulder month. Rains can start late. Herds are still mostly in the southern Serengeti. Good value if you can be flexible.

AprilWet

Long rains. Lush, quiet, and some camps close. Roads can be difficult. A poor month for a first safari.

MayWet

Rains continue, then ease. Migration starts to move. Low rates, and you need a tolerance for mud.

JuneStrong

Kenya dries. The western Serengeti corridor is often the place to be. The Mara starts to fill later in the month.

JulyPeak

High season. Herds are often in the northern Serengeti and beginning to reach the Mara. Book the Mara early.

AugustPeak

The busiest Mara month. Crossings are possible and not guaranteed. Amboseli is dry and good for elephants.

SeptemberPeak

Still a strong Mara month, with slightly fewer vehicles than August. Clear, dry viewing.

OctoberStrong

Crossings can continue early in the month. Short rains may begin late. A good month if you travel in the first half.

NovemberGood

Short rains, green scenery, fewer vehicles, lower rates. Herds start moving south. Birding is excellent.

DecemberPeak late

Rains ease, then the holidays push Mara prices up from mid-month. Southern Serengeti becomes relevant again late in the month.

The migration, without the slogan

The herds calve on the southern Serengeti around January and February. They move west toward the Grumeti around May and June, then north. Mara River crossings, on the Kenya or Tanzania bank, are most often looked for from July to October. By November the movement is south again. None of those sentences is a promise for a given week.
